title: Compose Plant lifecycle administration in the PWA

gates.name: admin_plant_lifecycle_browser
gates.command: cd frontend && npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/admin-plant-lifecycle.spec.ts

verify: Independent Boss/non-Boss browser verification covers Plant list/create/rename/archive/restore, no-op/conflict behavior, authoritative status, and no grant mutation.
evidence_required: FT-016-AC-014 RED: no Boss browser surface manages Plant lifecycle; GREEN: exact list/create/rename/archive/restore actions show backend-authoritative states while non-Boss, conflict, and safe-retry paths remain correct and grant rows are unchanged; decisive comparison: request/response/DOM plus Plant and grant reread; artifact: Plant-lifecycle evidence under .tasks/TASK-097-T3-FT-016-W3/.
purpose: Expose the accepted Plant lifecycle as one entity-lifecycle result without adopting Plant-access-grant administration.
success_outcome: A Boss can list and manage Plant create/name/archive/restore state through Plant Management HTTP with authoritative no-op/conflict results and no grant mutation.
anti_goals: Do not create/update/revoke PlantAccessGrant, manage Accounts/roles, or add new Plant states.
Do not make archived Plants operative or normally readable.

forbidden_scope: new Plant lifecycle states or restore side effects
stop_conditions: A lifecycle control needs a route outside Plant Management HTTP.
The UI would make archived state operative or infer conflict resolution.

constraints: Primary owner is Operator PWA; Access & Admin owns Plant lifecycle and audit writes.
Use exact lifecycle request fields and backend-selected current status.
invariants: Archived Plant remains non-operative until backend restore commits.
Lifecycle failure leaves Plant, grant, and audit state consistent.
verification_targets: FT-016-AC-014: Plant list/create/rename/archive/restore with authoritative no-op/conflict/non-Boss behavior and no grant mutation.
T3 harm proof uses isolated Plants and proves rejected/retried transitions leave no unintended state or audit effect.
